chapter: Style, the future of jazz and later playing
title: Touring Japan with the Ellington tribute band
summary: Mel Lewis, ill, leads Gunther Schuller's band; it lacked the Lincoln Center band's spark.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: In the late 1980s you went to Japan. Was it with – what band was that with?
That was on a Duke Ellington tribute.
Gunther Schuller put the orchestra together. He didn’t go on the tour. Mel Lewis was sort of the leader of the band.
What was Mel Lewis like to work with?
He was quite ill at that time.
Yeah, he was sick. Actually, I think he should not have been on the trip, because he was in such bad shape physically.
Had you played with him before?
Oh yeah. I played with Mel. We played on the – we used to do the Kraft Music Hall show together with Peter Matz.
What was that tour like, bringing Ellington to Japan?

It was nice. Most of these people in Japan, of course, they were mostly young people. It was well received, but the band was not a band of the quality of this Lincoln Center Orchestra. It was a good orchestra, first-rate players, but the feeling was a little different. They didn’t have the real Ellington spark that this band had. This band almost sounded – except for some of the improvisations, which were a little more modern in spots, it really sounded like the Ellington bands had.
